technical_and_design_decisions: Target Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
For reliable HDFS writes (U2), integrate HDFS flush/sync mechanisms with the message bus acknowledgement protocol to ensure end-to-end reliability.

For the new DSL parser (U5), decouple the parsing logic from the main application context to allow independent parsing of stream segments, enabling the Flo UI to validate modules and options without full context.
For single container deployment (U6), document an architecture where stream modules are loaded as isolated modules within a single JVM, leveraging Spring's classpath and resource management.
For ConfigurableConversionService (U7), implement a custom deserializer or post-processing hook to preserve non-default tuples.
assumptions: The developer has full access to the Spring XD / Spring Cloud Stream codebase and related repositories.
A test HDFS environment is available for validating reliable writes.
The Flo UI repository is accessible for parser integration and testing.
1 workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.
Existing CI/CD pipelines will be used for automated testing.

activities.activity_description: Experiment with the removal of the list of modules from BaseDefinition and implement reparse logic as needed (U1).
Implement the option of reliable HDFS writes for stream pipelines to get acknowledgement of actual HDFS commits (U2).
Add the ability to override the partition function within source or processor modules to send data to a specific partition (U3).
Implement the ability to consume multiple topic-partitions and serve the data via a single queue (U4).
Develop a new DSL parser to easily detect incorrect module/option values when supplied from the Flo UI, handling separate stream parsing (U5).
Design and document the approach towards deploying a stream in a single container with colocated modules (U6).
Handle non-default ConfigurableConversionService tuples in a uniform manner to prevent reset after deserialization (U7).
Benchmark a stream with and without JMX enabled, test in isolation, and document the performance differences (U8).
Perform integration testing across all new features, fix bugs, and prepare the increment for deployment.
